title: Grateful Dead Live at Yale Bowl, Yale University on 1971-07-31
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of the July 31, 1971 Yale Bowl show, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star‑Bird Song sequence and crisp, energetic performances.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑Charlie restoration delivers an excellent‑quality soundboard that showcases the raw, high‑energy vibe of the early ’71 Dead, with Bill Kreutzmann’s thunderous drums and tight band interplay. Standout moments include a smoking Dark Star → Bird Song medley, a celestial China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, and a rousing Uncle John’s Band/Johnny B. Goode finish. Overall the show is praised as one of the finest pre‑Keith, pre‑Mickey performances.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (10+) are 4–5 stars and emphasize both an exceptional performance and a high‑quality soundboard restoration, giving strong evidence for a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑restored SBD with minimal tape artifacts; drums and organ are clear; reviewers note the restoration work by Charlie as superb.

standout_songs: Dark Star → Bird Song (Playin' > Dark Star > Bird Song sequence)
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set builds through a powerful Playin'‑Dark Star‑Bird Song stretch, then moves into raw early‑71 material; the second set delivers classic jams and finishes with high‑octane rockers, giving the concert a cohesive, escalating momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Frequently jokes with the crowd, guitar work described as "on fire" and tightly leads the Dark Star jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass runs praised as powerful ("Phil paints Pollock"); solid foundation throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Guitar highlighted as painting "Picasso", energetic and forceful especially during jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann described as "out of control" with massive, well‑recorded fills that drive the performance.
